Register: "Eilersen Electric A/S"
Document: "Eilersen Electric Digital Systems A/S"

The document adds "Digital Systems" to the company name. Is this spelling drift or legal-suffix drift? No — "Digital Systems" is a substantive change to the company name, not a spelling variation or suffix drift.

Eilersen Electric A/S is a Danish load cell manufacturer. Eilersen Electric Digital Systems A/S — actually, the full legal name of the company is "Eilersen Electric Digital Systems A/S". Let me think. Eilersen Electric is a Danish company making load cells. Their legal name is indeed "Eilersen Electric Digital Systems A/S" (based in Ballerup, Denmark). Actually, checking my knowledge: Eilersen Electric A/S is commonly used, but the full registered name may be "Eilersen Electric Digital Systems A/S". Either way, this is the same company — the document's version is likely the full legal name while the register has a shortened form.

But per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity". Is this genuinely different? The rules don't include a category for abbreviated vs. full name. The options:
- same-entity: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences. Adding "Digital Systems" is not spelling drift or suffix drift... but it's clearly the same entity (a truncated vs full legal name).
- different-entity: genuinely different company. These aren't genuinely different companies — one is a shortened form of the other. Both refer to the same Danish load cell manufacturer.

The spirit of the rules: same-entity covers differences that don't change identity. "Eilersen Electric A/S" vs "Eilersen Electric Digital Systems A/S" — same company, the register likely truncated or used a trading name. The document is the legal instrument, so best_value should be the document's value if same-entity? Wait, rules say for same-entity, best_value isn't explicitly specified except for number/year formats ("same-entity with the register's canonical form"). For name same-entity cases, the examples given (spelling drift, suffix drift, accents) — presumably best_value from the document since the certificate is the legal instrument? The different-entity rule says best_value = document's because certificate is legal instrument. For same-entity names, it's ambiguous, but the principle "certificate is the legal instrument" suggests the document value would be preferred, unless it's a number format where register canonical form wins.

Given "Eilersen Electric Digital Systems A/S" is the fuller legal name appearing on the legal instrument, best_value = document's value seems right for same-entity.

Verdict: same-entity — the register's name is an abbreviation/short form of the document's full legal name; both refer to the same Danish manufacturer. Best value: "Eilersen Electric Digital Systems A/S".

Eilersen Electric A/S vs Eilersen Electric Digital Systems A/S — no, these are the same company; "Digital Systems" is part of the legal name. The certificate itself (OIML R60/2017-A-DK2-2021.01, issued by FORCE/DK2 in 2021) lists the applicant as Eilersen Electric Digital Systems A/S. So same entity.
